QF.id: AIFM CIII Legal Documents and Negotiations_1

question.text: Himalaya Arbitrage Fund, a Cat III AIF, is being constituted as a trust. Which of the following statements about the Trust Indenture is CORRECT from the legal-documentation perspective?

answer.text: The Trust Indenture can remain unregistered provided SEBI has registered the AIF under SEBI (AIF) Regulations, 2012.
The Trust Indenture is a registered document executed between the Trust Settlor and the Trustee and brings the trust into existence.
The Trust Indenture is signed only by the Investment Manager and the Sponsor; the Trustee is a mere observer.
The Trust Indenture is optional when the AIF uses a unified master-feeder structure at GIFT-IFSC.

explanation.text: The Logic: Per page 227, when a Cat III AIF is constituted as a trust, it is brought into existence through a Trust Indenture executed between the Trust Settlor and the Trustee. The trust deed is required to be registered, and the trust itself has no separate legal personality, so the registered indenture is the constitutional document. The Trap: Option A conflates SEBI AIF registration with registration of the trust deed under trust law; both are required. Option C wrongly drops the Trustee, who is in fact the counter-party to the Settlor in the indenture. Option D invents an IFSC carve-out that the source does not recognize. Note: Focus on the parties to the indenture (Settlor and Trustee), the registration requirement, and the fact that the trust has no separate legal personality.
